# isCellGridRange

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a single-cell range.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isCellGridRange() — Checks whether a value is a single-cell range. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isCellGridRange(gridRange: GridRange): boolean;
```

One row and one column, measured by the bounds rather than by how the range was written: the end indices are exclusive, so a single cell is `endRowIndex - startRowIndex === 1` and the same for the columns. A range with a bound left out is open in that direction and is never a single cell.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter   | Type        | Description                                      |
| :---------- | :---------- | :----------------------------------------------- |
| `gridRange` | `GridRange` | The [`GridRange`](GridRange.md) object to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a single-cell range; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isCellGridRange({ startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 1, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 1 }); // => true
isCellGridRange({ startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 2, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 1 }); // => false
isCellGridRange({}); // => false
isCellGridRange(null); // => false
```
